1	package versioncheck
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7		"io"
8		"os"
9	
10		"charm.land/huh/v2"
11	
12		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/interactive"
13		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
14		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/uiform"
15	)
16	
17	// envKillSwitch disables the interactive update prompt regardless of TTY.
18	const envKillSwitch = "ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE"
19	
20	// AutoUpdateAction describes the result of an update prompt.
21	type AutoUpdateAction string
22	
23	const (
24		autoUpdateActionSkip                 AutoUpdateAction = "skip"
25		autoUpdateActionUpdate               AutoUpdateAction = "update"
26		autoUpdateActionSkipUntilNextVersion AutoUpdateAction = "skip_until_next_version"
27	)
28	
29	// chooseUpdateFn is the signature for the update-prompt seam. The
30	// concrete implementation renders a huh.Select with the installer
31	// command interpolated into option 1.
32	type chooseUpdateFn func(ctx context.Context, currentVersion, latestVersion, cmdStr string) (AutoUpdateAction, error)
33	
34	// Test seams.
35	var (
36		runInstaller                 = realRunInstaller
37		chooseUpdate  chooseUpdateFn = realChooseUpdate
38		isTerminalOut                = interactive.IsTerminalWriter
39	)
40	
41	// maybeAutoUpdate prints an update notification and offers an interactive
42	// upgrade. Silent on every failure path — it must never interrupt the CLI.
43	//
44	// The same 3-option prompt (update / skip / skip until next version) is
45	// shown for every install manager that supports auto-installation
46	// (brew, mise, curl-bash). The only thing that varies between
47	// installers is the shell command interpolated into option 1.
48	//
49	// If the installer command fails, a hint with the exact command is
50	// printed so the user can retry manually. The 24h version-check cache
51	// is not invalidated on failure: we don't want to re-prompt on every
52	// invocation while an upstream issue (network, auth, repo outage) is
53	// still in place.
54	//
55	// When the prompt cannot be shown (kill switch set, or non-interactive
56	// environment like CI / agent subprocess / no TTY) the installer
57	// command is printed so the user still learns what to run manually.
58	//
59	// On Windows the installer is never auto-run (a running entire.exe cannot
60	// replace itself), so scoop, mise, and install.ps1 commands are printed
61	// for the user to run once entire has exited.
62	func maybeAutoUpdate(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer, currentVersion, latestVersion string) AutoUpdateAction {
63		cmdStr := UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary(currentVersion)
64	
65		// Windows can't replace a running executable, so no installer can update
66		// entire in place while it runs. For Scoop this is acute: the live
67		// entire.exe holds its own shim open, so scoop can't relink or uninstall it
68		// mid-run (install leaves the shim on the old package, and uninstall fails
69		// with "still running"). Never auto-run on Windows — print the command(s)
70		// to run once entire has exited.
71		//
72		// This returns plain skip, not skipUntilNextVersion, so Windows users can't
73		// suppress a specific version: the nudge returns every 24h until they
74		// update. That is deliberate while the Scoop rename migration is live —
75		// there is no prompt to choose from, so there is no choice to remember.
76		if !installerAutoRuns {
77			printNotification(w, currentVersion, latestVersion)
78			fmt.Fprintf(w, "To update, run the following in PowerShell when entire is not running:\n  %s\n", cmdStr)
79			return autoUpdateActionSkip
80		}
81	
82		if os.Getenv(envKillSwitch) != "" || !interactive.CanPromptInteractively() || !isTerminalOut(w) {
83			printNotification(w, currentVersion, latestVersion)
84			fmt.Fprintf(w, "To update, run:\n  %s\n", cmdStr)
85			return autoUpdateActionSkip
86		}
87	
88		action, err := chooseUpdate(ctx, currentVersion, latestVersion, cmdStr)
89		if err != nil {
90			logging.Debug(ctx, "auto-update: prompt failed", "error", err.Error())
91			return autoUpdateActionSkip
92		}
93	
94		switch action {
95		case autoUpdateActionUpdate:
96			fmt.Fprintf(w, "\nUpdating Entire CLI: %s\n", cmdStr)
97			if err := runInstaller(ctx, cmdStr); err != nil {
98				fmt.Fprintf(w, "Update failed: %v\nTry again later running:\n  %s\n", err, cmdStr)
99				return autoUpdateActionUpdate
100			}
101			fmt.Fprintln(w, "Update complete. Re-run entire to use the new version.")
102			return autoUpdateActionUpdate
103		case autoUpdateActionSkipUntilNextVersion:
104			return autoUpdateActionSkipUntilNextVersion
105		case autoUpdateActionSkip:
106			return autoUpdateActionSkip
107		default:
108			return autoUpdateActionSkip
109		}
110	}
111	
112	// realChooseUpdate renders a huh.Select with the three update actions.
113	// In normal mode this is an arrow-key TUI; when ACCESSIBLE is set huh
114	// falls back to a plain numbered prompt readable by screen readers.
115	func realChooseUpdate(ctx context.Context, currentVersion, latestVersion, cmdStr string) (AutoUpdateAction, error) {
116		action := autoUpdateActionUpdate
117		sel := huh.NewSelect[AutoUpdateAction]().
118			Title(fmt.Sprintf("Update available! %s -> %s",
119				displayVersion(currentVersion), displayVersion(latestVersion))).
120			Description("Release notes: "+releaseNotesURL(latestVersion)).
121			Options(
122				huh.NewOption(fmt.Sprintf("Update now (runs `%s`)", cmdStr), autoUpdateActionUpdate),
123				huh.NewOption("Skip", autoUpdateActionSkip),
124				huh.NewOption("Skip until next version", autoUpdateActionSkipUntilNextVersion),
125			).
126			Value(&action)
127		form := uiform.New(huh.NewGroup(sel))
128		if err := form.RunWithContext(ctx); err != nil {
129			if errors.Is(err, huh.ErrUserAborted) || errors.Is(err, huh.ErrTimeout) {
130				return autoUpdateActionSkip, nil
131			}
132			return autoUpdateActionSkip, fmt.Errorf("update prompt: %w", err)
133		}
134		return action, nil
135	}

Description:
Problem: The previous version pointed Windows users to the releases download page when their install location didn't match a known package manager (Scoop, mise). The POSIX curl-bash fallback couldn't run on Windows, leaving no automated install path for unknown install locations.
Solution: Replace the downloads-page fallback with the README's install.ps1 one-liners: bare irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex when there is nothing to pass, otherwise iex "& {$(irm https://entire.io/install.ps1)} -InstallDir '<dir of the running entire.exe>' -NoPathUpdate" (nightly adds -Channel nightly) so the installer replaces the binary in place without rewriting the user PATH. The path's $ and backtick are escaped for the double-quoted string and a quote is doubled. An explicit -InstallDir opts out of the installer's Scoop-first default (#2152, 322b4bf18). On Windows the command is printed for the user to run in PowerShell after entire exits, since a running entire.exe cannot replace itself and irm | iex does not paste into cmd.exe.
Install detection is split into per-OS probe files (brew and mise on unix; Scoop and mise on Windows) so the runtime GOOS switch is gone. Every OS has an update command, so the auto-install predicate was removed. Scoop and mise probes honor relocated install roots (SCOOP, SCOOP_GLOBAL, Scoop's config.json root_path/global_path, MISE_INSTALLS_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR) with case-insensitive matching on Windows. The installer runner is per-OS too; the Windows stub deliberately does not shell through cmd.exe because the PowerShell one-liners would be split on | and &.

I validated, and one thing was genuinely wrong — I fixed it rather than sending it back, because the fixes were mine, not `autoupdate`'s.

**The mix-up first:** `autoupdate [142f98]` is the same session as `uninstall-ext-ps1-autoupdate-ac` (same socket, renamed). It was the *reviewer* — it wrote both findings and sent them to me; I wrote both fixes an hour ago. So there was no one to hand work back to; validating meant reviewing my own commits against its finding text, which is what I did.

**What held up:** finding 1's coverage is complete. `UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary` has exactly two printers — `maybeAutoUpdate`'s Windows branch and the checkpoint-policy message — and because `commandShell` is a required parameter rather than an option, no future caller can print the command without naming a shell.

**What did not:** the isolation fix was half-closed. `miseRoots()` reads `MISE_INSTALLS_DIR`/`MISE_DATA_DIR` on the same `UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary` call that `scoopRoots()` reads the Scoop env, and neither Windows table cleared them. The Scoop rows were safe (Scoop probe runs first), but the three install.ps1 rows — `C:\tools\cli`, `C:\Users\test\.local\bin`, `C:\Program Files\Entire` — resolve to `miseUpgradeCmd` on a host whose mise root prefixes them. Same class as the accepted finding, weaker odds. `7f25257b2` renames the helper to `isolateWindowsInstallEnv` and clears both mise vars.

Branch `feat/windows-ps1-autoupdate` is now at `7f25257b2` (three commits unpushed). `GOOS=windows` vet and test-binary build clean, versioncheck/checkpointpolicy/strategy pass, lint 0 issues.

One limit worth repeating, since both the reviewer and I hit it: nothing on this machine has *run* the Windows-tagged tests, only compiled them. Whether the isolation actually works needs the Windows CI job.
